title: Fundamental Rights — scheme of Part III

content.overview: Part III of the Constitution, Articles 12 to 35, guarantees justiciable Fundamental Rights, primarily against the State defined in Article 12. Article 13 deals with laws inconsistent with those rights. The rights are grouped as equality (Articles 14 to 18), freedoms (Article 19), life, liberty, protection in criminal law, education and arrest (Articles 20 to 22 and 21A), exploitation (Articles 23 and 24), religion (Articles 25 to 28), culture and education (Articles 29 and 30), and constitutional remedies (Article 32). Articles 33 to 35 deal with modification for the armed forces, martial law, and legislation. Article 31 as a fundamental right to property was omitted by the Forty-fourth Amendment; property is now Article 300A.
content.study: Start with Articles 12, 13 and 32. Then match the facts to one article. Do not treat Part IV as Part III. Do not plead repealed Article 31 as a living fundamental right.

sections.heading: Who is bound
sections.body: Generally the State under Article 12. Instrumentality and agency tests decide whether bodies beyond government and legislatures are other authorities. Horizontal application is exceptional and must be pleaded from settled case law, not assumed.

sections.heading: Enforceability
sections.body: Article 32 is itself a Fundamental Right — move the Supreme Court for Part III enforcement. Article 226 is the High Court writ power (Fundamental Rights and for any other purpose); it is not itself a Fundamental Right. See also the PIL subject set for standing practice.

sections.heading: FR and DPSPs
sections.body: Fundamental Rights are justiciable; Directive Principles are not enforceable by courts (Article 37). Courts seek harmony where possible (Minerva Mills). Do not write that DPSPs always yield to FR, or the reverse.

sections.heading: Historical property
sections.body: Article 31 as a Fundamental Right was omitted by the Constitution (Forty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1978. Articles 31A–31C remain material savings. Current property protection is Article 300A (not Part III).

learningObjectives: Map Part III from Articles 12 to 35.
Identify who is bound and how a right is enforced.
Keep property and Directive Principles outside living Part III rights.
enhancement.definition: Fundamental Rights are the justiciable guarantees in Part III, enforceable against the State and, where the article says so, against other persons.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: A Part III claim needs a right, a duty-bearer within the article, and a remedy under Article 32 or 226. Article 13 is the inconsistency rule, not itself a right.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: Constitution of India, Articles 12 to 35. Article 226 is the High Court interface. Article 300A is the present property clause.
essentialIngredients: State or other duty-bearer within that article
Law or action inconsistent with the right
Article 13 if a law is challenged
Horizontal articles used only where the text reaches private persons
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Part III is enforceable. Article 12 defines the State for Part III unless the context otherwise requires. Article 13 says laws inconsistent with Part III are void to the extent of the inconsistency, and it defines law to include orders, bye-laws, rules, regulations, notifications and custom or usage having the force of law. Most rights run against the State. Articles 15(2), 17, 23 and 24 also reach other persons in the terms those articles use. Article 32 is itself a fundamental right to move the Supreme Court. The Forty-fourth Amendment removed Article 31 and Article 19(1)(f). A current property complaint is Article 300A, not Part III, unless a savings article such as 31A, 31B or 31C is actually in issue.
examples: A statute denies a Part III right. Article 13 and the specific right are pleaded, with Article 32 or 226 as the remedy.
A private employer is sued under Article 14. Article 14 binds the State, so Article 12 must be met unless another article applies.
A landowner pleads Article 31 as a fundamental right after the Forty-fourth Amendment. That article is omitted.
enhancement.problemApplication: Name the article, test Article 12, check whether the right is vertical or also horizontal, and choose Article 32 or 226. Do not use Part IV as the cause of action.
distinctions: Article 12 State vs a private person
enhancement.caseLawNotes: No new case citation or ratio was added. Names already in the published overview are not promoted to verified holdings.
enhancement.shortAnswerStructure: Part III, Articles 12 to 35, justiciable mainly against the State, with Article 32 as the Supreme Court remedy.
enhancement.tenMarkStructure: Articles 12 and 13 → groups of rights → Article 32 → property and Part IV excluded.
enhancement.sixteenMarkStructure: Scheme of Part III → State and law → each cluster → horizontal exceptions → remedies → Articles 33 to 35 → omitted property right → facts → conclusion.

keyTakeaways: Article 13 voids inconsistent laws to the extent of inconsistency.
Article 32 enforces Part III in the Supreme Court.
Article 31 is no longer a fundamental right.
